title: Embrace
surface:
He crossed a line he should not have crossed. She came against the entire crowd. Their “embrace” jolted me awake.
At the fork ahead, someone else suddenly stopped to wait. In my panic, I gave him an “embrace” too.
Why did nobody find these encounters heartwarming?
solution: These were traffic collisions. One driver changed lanes across a solid line while another drove the wrong way; their cars collided. The noise woke the narrator, who was driving while drowsy. A different car ahead stopped abruptly after missing a motorway exit. The narrator panicked, pressed the accelerator instead of the brake and rear-ended it. Both “embraces” were crashes. The stopped driver was not waiting to greet anyone.

facts.text: An illegal lane change and a wrong-way driver cause the first collision, waking the drowsy narrator.
A different car stops near an exit; the narrator presses the wrong pedal and hits it. Both embraces are car collisions.
The narrator is not part of the first two-car collision; the second collision involves a separate stopped car.
The car ahead stops after missing an exit, not to wait for the narrator.

unknowns: Injuries, speeds, vehicle models and the aftermath are unspecified.
character_claims: “Stopped to wait” is the narrator’s figurative description, not the other driver’s actual intention.
hints: Consider traffic meanings for crossing a line and moving against everyone else.
Both embraces are noisy collisions; the narrator is moving too.
One crash wakes a driver, who then hits a car stopped near an exit.
